summary: The article accurately reports on the RBI's recent monetary policy decisions and outlook, with most factual claims verified by authoritative sources.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently kept its main interest rate, the repo rate, unchanged at 5.25%.
claims.note: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) unanimously decided to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its meeting held from August 3 to 5, 2026.

claims.claim: minutes of this meeting were released last week, they revealed a significant shift in thinking among the central bank's top officials.
claims.note: The minutes of the MPC meeting from August 3-5, 2026, were released on August 19, 2026, and indicated concerns about rising inflation and the possibility of future rate hikes.

claims.claim: India's retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July 2026, up from 4.38% in June, staying above the RBI's medium-term target of 4%.
claims.note: India's retail inflation rate increased to 4.45% in July 2026 from 4.38% in June 2026. This is above the RBI's medium-term target of 4%.

claims.claim: members, including Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta, explicitly stated that "a case for a hike may emerge during the course of the year" if inflation continues to rise, especially with headline inflation projected to peak at 5.9% in Q3 FY27.
claims.note: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated in the MPC minutes that a case for a rate hike might emerge if headline inflation peaks at 5.9% in Q3 FY27.

claims.claim: The RBI has a mandate to keep retail inflation between 2% and 6%, with a sweet spot target of 4%.
claims.note: The Indian government, in consultation with the RBI, set an inflation target of 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2%, meaning the target range is 2-6%.

claims.claim: Food inflation climbed to 5.52% in July 2026.
claims.note: Provisional food inflation based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI) stood at 5.52% year-on-year in July 2026.

claims.claim: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) typically meets six times a year, every two months, to review the economic situation and decide on monetary policy.
claims.note: While the RBI Act mandates at least four MPC meetings a year, the RBI typically conducts these meetings on a bi-monthly basis, resulting in six meetings annually.
